run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The only index on the Elasticsearch target is app-263-prod-logs (7 documents, all returned), and it holds log lines from three region-suffixed payment services, not from a service named exactly "payment-service": ERROR 4 / INFO 2 / WARN 1, with payment-service-us 3, payment-service-ap 2, payment-service-eu 2. Four ERROR lines are visible: payment-service-eu failed to authenticate to adyen-eu with an invalid api_key at 05:04:57Z; payment-service-us reported its connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50) at the same instant; at 04:04:57Z payment-service-us logged a 30s upstream timeout to stripe-us and payment-service-eu logged adyen-eu sandbox 503 Service Unavailable; at 05:34:57Z payment-service-us logged WARN retry queue depth=812. The documents carry no HTTP status field, so the 500s themselves are not recorded, and the leading explanations (credential fault at payment-service-eu; upstream processor faults; connection-pool saturation as a consequence of hung upstream calls) remain hypotheses. Prometheus and Jaeger answered SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on four attempts, so error-rate metrics and traces are unknown. In the Kubernetes cluster production-eu-west-2 the only visible payment workload is Deployment otel-demo/payment (1/1 ready, image 2.0.2-payment), whose pod completed charges before and after an unexplained single container restart (exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finished 04:23:42Z); its flagd payment flags are off, so fault injection is rejected for that workload. That workload is a different entity from the payment-service-us/eu/ap services in the index, so its successful charges neither confirm nor clear the indexed services. No single fault object is established, so root_cause is null.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target exposes exactly one index, app-263-prod-logs, with docs.count 7; a match_all aggregation over the authorized window returned 7 documents with level buckets ERROR=4, INFO=2, WARN=1 and service buckets payment-service-us=3, payment-service-ap=2, payment-service-eu=2.

All 7 documents in app-263-prod-logs were returned for the authorized window; the only error/warn messages present are: payment-service-us "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms" (ERROR, 2026-11-21T04:04:57Z), payment-service-eu "adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable" (ERROR, 2026-11-21T04:04:57Z), payment-service-us "Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)" (ERROR, 2026-11-21T05:04:57Z), payment-service-eu "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" (ERROR, 2026-11-21T05:04:57Z) and payment-service-us "Retry queue depth=812" (WARN, 2026-11-21T05:34:57Z).

The app-263-prod-logs mapping defines only the fields level, message, service and timestamp; no field carrying an HTTP status code exists in the mapping, so the 500 status codes mentioned in the question are not recorded in these documents.
payment-service-ap is the only regional service with non-error readings in the index: INFO "Healthy: p95 latency 290ms" at 2026-11-21T04:04:57Z and INFO "Healthy" at 2026-11-21T05:34:57Z.

In cluster production-eu-west-2 the only payment deployment is otel-demo/payment with 1 replica, 1 ready and 1 available, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment; its pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d is Running, owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6, restartCount 1, with last termination exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z.

The pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d restarted its container in place: the new instance logged "start" and "node --require ./opentelemetry.js index.js" at 2026-11-21T04:23:50Z and "payment gRPC server started on port 8080" at 04:23:52Z, then completed charge requests (msg "Transaction complete.") at 04:25:26Z, 04:25:48Z, 04:26:33Z, 04:27:34Z, 04:28:23Z and 04:29:07Z.

The previous container instance of payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged its last line at 2026-11-21T04:07:21.702Z (msg "Transaction complete.") and produced no further stdout/stderr lines before the fetch window ended at 04:23:00Z; the previous instance's earlier output likewise contains normal charge handling and no error text.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) declares paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable") with state ENABLED and defaultVariant "off"; the deployment otel-demo/payment sets no processor credentials, only OTEL_*, PAYMENT_PORT, FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT.

The cross-namespace event grouping returned within the window (source timestamps 2026-11-21T05:28:04Z to 06:00:26Z) contains only involvedObject namespace app-101: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet=2, Pod Created=3/Killing=2/Pulled=3/Scheduled=2/Started=3, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate=2, Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint=1; no otel-demo event group was returned.

Leading hypothesis for payment-service-eu: the ERROR line "Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key" (2026-11-21T05:04:57Z) is the deepest cause visible for that service's failed charge requests, i.e. a credential/configuration fault at the adyen-eu integration rather than a transient network problem; the api_key value itself could not be read, so the credential state is unverified.

Alternative hypothesis: external processor faults drive the failures — payment-service-eu's "adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable" and payment-service-us's "Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms" (both 2026-11-21T04:04:57Z) — but only four ERROR lines exist and no processor-side data is available to confirm the processors' own state.

Alternative hypothesis: payment-service-us is locally saturated — "Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)" followed by WARN "Retry queue depth=812" — which would fail concurrent charge requests; the pool message is equally consistent with a downstream consequence of the stripe-us 30s timeouts holding connections, and the evidence cannot order the two.

The cluster workload named payment is not shown failing: otel-demo/payment is 1/1 ready, and its pod's own logs show successful "Transaction complete." charges before (04:00:03Z–04:07:21Z) and after (04:25:26Z–04:29:07Z) the 04:23:42Z container restart; this entity differs from the payment-service-us/eu/ap services in the index, so it neither corroborates nor clears them.

Fault injection through the flagd feature flags paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable is rejected as the cause for the otel-demo/payment workload: both flags declare defaultVariant "off", and the pod kept completing charges; for the indexed payment-service-us/eu/ap services no feature-flag or fault-injection setting is visible at all, so this mechanism is unverified there rather than confirmed.

Human follow-up: verify and, if rejected, re-provision the adyen-eu API credential used by payment-service-eu (the value cannot be read here), and confirm with the adyen-eu and stripe-us providers whether their 503/timeout episodes at 04:04:57Z were theirs, before attributing the 500s to either.

Human follow-up: capture payment-service HTTP status/dependency metrics and traces (the Prometheus and Jaeger sources were unreachable in this Run) so that the 500 rate, the p95 latency and the pool-active gauge can be tied to these log lines, and check whether the pool limit of 50 and the 30s stripe timeout need tuning.

gaps: No document in app-263-prod-logs matches the exact service name "payment-service": a match_phrase query on service="payment-service" returned 0 documents (status no_data); the only service values present are payment-service-us, payment-service-ap and payment-service-eu.

The index holds only 7 documents (docs.count 7, all returned), all timestamped between 2026-11-21T04:04:57Z and 05:34:57Z at three sample instants; error onset before 04:04:57Z, persistence after 05:34:57Z and any errors in the remaining ~22 hours of the window are unknown.

The documents record no HTTP status code (mapping has only level, message, service, timestamp), so the stated 500 responses are not directly observed; the level=ERROR lines are the only failure evidence.

Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_label_values, traces_search and traces_list_services all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on repeated attempts, so payment error-rate, latency and span-status data are unknown, not zero.

The adyen-eu api_key value and any credential/config object behind the "invalid api_key" line are not readable (secrets are not accessible), so the credential state of payment-service-eu could not be verified.

The otel-demo/payment container restart is unexplained: the previous instance's last log line is 04:07:21.702Z, termination is recorded as exitCode 255 reason Unknown at 04:23:42Z with no OOMKilled/Evicted mark, and the events read cover only 05:28:04Z–06:00:26Z and only app-101 objects, so no otel-demo event explains the restart and it is left as an unresolved change in the window.

No Kubernetes objects named payment-service, payment-service-us, payment-service-eu or payment-service-ap exist in the readable cluster (the only payment Service is otel-demo/payment on port 8080), so the objects behind the indexed services are unknown.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no deployment/config change can be tied to the 04:04:57Z or 05:04:57Z errors.
next_steps: Verify the adyen-eu credential/configuration for payment-service-eu against the credential store and check whether the api_key was rotated or revoked before 05:04:57Z.
Obtain adyen-eu and stripe-us incident/status history for 2026-11-21 04:04:57Z to confirm or drop the upstream-processor hypothesis.
Restore or point the investigation at a working Prometheus and Jaeger so payment-service error-rate, rpc status codes and pool/queue metrics can be evaluated.
Review the payment-service-us connection pool size (max=50) and the 30s stripe-us client timeout, and check whether pool exhaustion coincides with the retry-queue backlog after the timeouts.
